rationale: A is the more polished and better-choreographed site: a rising moon, a pinned phone that changes through three phases, and a status pill that runs from 9:41 PM to first light with a sunrise at the download section, but its headline flashes at 80 ms then goes blank until ~1.3 s, a few scroll frames are half-empty (5323, 6679), and the dark purple gradient, serif-italic accents, glass bento and pricing cards read as a familiar premium AI-app template. B is built around the brief: a contour-chart hero with a time axis and a 'bulletin for tonight', a hypnogram motif reused as logo, scroll-linked mix dashboard and testimonial signatures, a sleep-stage data table with citations, six real app screens, a comparison-table pricing layout and a wake-time calculator, across colour-blocked sections with wave dividers. B's weaknesses are a hero that is still blank at 80 ms and only starts revealing after 2 s, a desktop hero headline set in a plainer wide sans than the condensed face used elsewhere, a CTA that still looks greyed at 3 s, and a pink hypnogram line crossing the headline on mobile. B's hover states (pink fills, logo colour swap, underlines) are clearer than A's very subtle glows; B wins narrowly on originality and content design over A's finish and motion.
